summary: Catharine Bird Runkle was an Indologist. She studied at Radcliffe College in 1886 under Charles Rockwell Lanman.

Catherine Bell was a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. She studied under Joseph M. Kitagawa at the University of Chicago (~1977–1983) and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Cornille works in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees at KU Leuven (1979–1984, 1986–1989) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1984–1986), later holding faculty appointments at KU Leuven, College of the Holy Cross, and Boston College.
Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was an Indologist and historian. She completed her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1977–1984) and served there as an Assistant Professor from ~1986 to 2021.

Catherine Ludvik works in religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse, Antonino Forte, and Werner Knobl, later teaching at Stanford, Doshisha, and Kyoto Sangyo universities, among other research appointments.

Catherine Prueitt works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Rochester and Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, later serving on the faculties of George Mason University and the University of British Columbia.
Cathy Cantwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kent (~1985–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Cambridge under E. B. Cowell and Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and the University of Cambridge.

Cecil Henry Bompas was an Indologist. He was educated at Westminster School and Trinity College, Cambridge, and served in the Indian Civil Service (1887–1923), the Bengal Legislative Council (1916), and the Calcutta Improvement Trust (1920).

Cecil Jermyn Brown was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Oxford, he taught at Canning College (1909–1920) and the University of Lucknow (1921–1926) and was a Fellow at the University of Allahabad (1919–1921).

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held academic posts at Yale University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia, where he was Professor of English from ~1970 to 1991.
Cezary Galewicz is an Indologist who held posts at Jagiellonian University as Adjunct Professor (attested 2012) and Professor (2015).

Ch'ing-mao Cheng was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who studied at National Taiwan University and Princeton University. He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Massachusetts Amherst, and was Founding Chair at National Dong Hwa University.

Chack-fan Lee studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Western Ontario. Active in Buddhist studies and other fields, he served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaesong Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1995) under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at Hebrew University, SOAS, and Oxford. He served as a lecturer at SOAS (1938–1941), Cowley Lecturer at Oxford (1943–1956), and Associate Professor at Hebrew University (1956–1985).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at Oxford and held posts at Oxford, Cambridge, the National University of Singapore, and Lancaster University, where he became Distinguished Professor.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit works in religious and Buddhist studies. After earning a BA at Chulalongkorn University, he served there as a part-time instructor and as a professor in the Faculty of Social Science at Kasetsart University (both attested 2012).
